question: During which of the following editions of the National Finite Element Developers’ meeting did Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) unveil the latest version of Finite Element Analysis of Structures (FEAST) software in February 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** unveiled the latest version of its indigenous structural analysis software, **FEAST (Finite Element Analysis of Structures)**, during the **8th edition** of the **National Finite Element Developers’ Meeting (NFEDM)**.
 
• The event was held in **February 2025** at the **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)** located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, Kerala.
 
• The **8th NFEDM** brought together experts, researchers, and developers from across the country to discuss advancements in **computational mechanics** and structural engineering.
 
• The release of the latest **FEAST** version is a significant milestone in India's pursuit of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the domain of sophisticated engineering software.
 
• The software is designed to provide a robust and cost-effective alternative to expensive foreign-made **Finite Element Analysis (FEA)** tools, reducing dependency on international licenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About FEAST Software:**
 
 
• **FEAST** stands for **Finite Element Analysis of Structures**. It is a comprehensive software package developed by **VSSC/ISRO** for **linear** and **non-linear** structural analysis.
 
• It is used to analyze the structural integrity of **rockets**, **satellites**, and **launch vehicles**, ensuring they can withstand the extreme forces experienced during space missions.
 
• The software supports a wide range of applications, including **static**, **dynamic**, **thermal**, and **buckling** analysis of complex structures.
 
• It is available in various versions, such as **Academic** (for students), **Premium** (for small-scale industries), and **Professional** (for large enterprises).
 
 
 
• **National Finite Element Developers’ Meeting (NFEDM):**
 
 
• The **NFEDM** is a biennial or periodic national-level platform initiated to foster collaboration among **Indian developers** of structural analysis tools.
 
• It aims to create a unified ecosystem for **Finite Element Method (FEM)** development in India, encouraging the use of indigenous technologies in **aerospace**, **defense**, and **civil engineering**.
 
 
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC):**
 
 
• Located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **VSSC** is the lead center of **ISRO** responsible for the design and development of launch vehicle technology.
 
• It was named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, the father of the Indian space program, and has been instrumental in developing the **SLV-3**, **ASLV**, **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Significance:** The development of **FEAST** by **ISRO** scientists highlights India's capability to produce high-end **Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE)** software that meets global standards.
 
• **Date and Timeline:** The **8th NFEDM** took place in **February 2025**, marking several years of continuous evolution since the initial versions of the software were conceptualized.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By utilizing **indigenous software**, Indian industries and academic institutions can save millions in **foreign exchange** that would otherwise be spent on proprietary software like **ANSYS** or **NASTRAN**.
 
• **User Base:** Beyond **ISRO**, the software is being increasingly adopted by the **Indian Navy**, **defense labs (DRDO)**, and several **IITs** and **NITs** for research and development purposes.
